evidence.quote: Here a convex body is compact with nonempty interior, and $\det\Lambda$ denotes lattice covolume.

There is an absolute constant $C>0$ such that, for every integer $n\ge2$ and every convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$, one full-rank lattice $\Lambda$ satisfies $$K+\Lambda=\mathbb R^n,\qquad
 \frac{\operatorname{vol}_n(K)}{\det\Lambda}\le Cn\log n.$$ No symmetry or boundary regularity is assumed.

exclusions.query: Coverage of nonconvex, unbounded, or lower-dimensional footprints.
exclusions.reason: The guarantee requires a compact convex body with nonempty interior in the stated ambient dimension.

hypotheses.statement:
There is an absolute constant $C>0$ such that, for every integer $n\ge2$ and every convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$, one full-rank lattice $\Lambda$ satisfies $$K+\Lambda=\mathbb R^n,\qquad
 \frac{\operatorname{vol}_n(K)}{\det\Lambda}\le Cn\log n.$$ No symmetry or boundary regularity is assumed.

There are absolute constants $c,C>0$ with the following property. Fix $M\ge1$. For all sufficiently large $n$, with threshold depending only on $M$, suppose that $D$ is a positive integer and $$1\le D,R\le M(1+\log\log n)^M,\qquad m=n-D.$$ Every convex body in $\mathbb R^n$ has an invertible affine image $K\subset\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^D$ and a list of at most $(Cm^2)^D$ convex bodies $J_a\subset\mathbb R^m$ such that, writing $K_y=\{x:(x,y)\in K\}$, for every $\|y\|\le R$ some label $a$ satisfies $$J_a\subset K_y,
 \qquad
 c\,\operatorname{vol}_n(K)\gamma_D(y)
 \le \operatorname{vol}_m(J_a)
 \le C\,\operatorname{vol}_n(K)\gamma_D(y).
 \label{eq:section-labels}$$

Let $J_1,\ldots,J_N$ be convex bodies in $\mathbb R^m$, let $D_h>0$, and set $u_a=\operatorname{vol}_m(J_a)/D_h$. If $$\max_a u_a\le\eta_m,
 \qquad
 (1+C_{\mathrm R})\sum_{a=1}^N e^{-u_a/2}<1,
 \label{eq:horizontal-criterion}$$ there is a lattice $\Lambda_h$ of determinant $D_h$ satisfying $$h_{\Lambda_h}(J_a)\le e^{-u_a/2}
 \qquad (1\le a\le N).
 \label{eq:horizontal-holes}$$ In particular, this conclusion holds for all sufficiently large $m$ if $$\min_a u_a\ge\sqrt m,\qquad
 \max_a u_a=o(m),\qquad
 \log N=o(\sqrt m).$$ The dimension threshold in this last formulation depends only on the three numerical bounds, not on the shapes of the bodies.

For every sufficiently large $b$, there is a prime $p_b$ satisfying $$b\mu_b-4b^{0.56}\le\log p_b\le b\mu_b-3b^{0.56}.
 \label{eq:block-prime}$$ Let $G_b=\mathbb F_{p_b}^b$, and associate with $z\in G_b$ the anchor $t_z=z/p_b\in[0,1)^b$, using the representatives $0,\ldots,p_b-1$ in every coordinate. Define the eligible set $E_b\subset G_b$ by the two conditions $$\left|\log F_b(t_z)-b\mu_b\right|\le b^{0.56},\qquad
 \#\left\{j:\left|t_{z,j}-\frac12\right|\le h_b^{-2}\right\}
       \ge b^{0.70}.
 \label{eq:block-eligible}$$ Then $$\mathbb E_{z\in G_b}F_b(t_z)=1+O(b^{-1/20}),\qquad
 \mathbb E_{z\in G_b}F_b(t_z)\mathbf 1_{E_b}(z)=1+O(b^{-1/20}).
 \label{eq:block-mass}$$ Moreover, $\mu_b=\log h_b+O(1)$. Put $\eta_b=bh_b^2/p_b$. If $t$ belongs to the grid cell $Q_z=t_z+[0,p_b^{-1})^b$, then, for every $\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}^b$, $$\begin{split}
 e^{-\eta_b}F_b(t_z)&\le F_b(t)\le e^{\eta_b}F_b(t_z),\\
 e^{-\eta_b}\frac{F_b(t_z)}{p_b}P_{b,t_z}(\varepsilon)
 &\le\frac{h_b^b}{p_b}\gamma_b\bigl(h_b(t-\varepsilon)\bigr)
 \le e^{\eta_b}\frac{F_b(t_z)}{p_b}P_{b,t_z}(\varepsilon).
 \end{split}
 \label{eq:block-rounding}$$ There is an absolute $c>0$ such that, for every eligible $z$, every $t\in Q_z$, and every $\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}^b$, $$\frac{F_b(t_z)}{p_b}P_{b,t_z}(\varepsilon)\le e^{-c b^{0.70}},
 \qquad
 \frac{h_b^b}{p_b}\gamma_b\bigl(h_b(t-\varepsilon)\bigr)
       \le e^{-c b^{0.70}}.
 \label{eq:block-atom}$$

There are absolute constants $A,B>0$ with the following property. Let $b\ge B$ be an integer, and use the objects in Lemma 6. Suppose that $H$ is a finite abelian group, $\log|H|\le b^4$, and $g_0:H\to[0,\infty)$ satisfies $$\frac12\le\bar g_0:=\mathbb E_{x\in H}g_0(x)\le2,\qquad g_0(x)\le\exp(5a^{0.56})\quad(x\in H)$$ for some $1\le a\le b^{1/0.9}$. Then one can choose shifts $w_1,\ldots,w_b\in H$, a usable set $U_b\subset E_b$, and a one-dimensional linear subspace $C_b\subset G_b$ such that, writing $W\varepsilon=\sum_{j=1}^b\varepsilon_jw_j$, $$\sum_{\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}^b}P_{b,t_z}(\varepsilon)g_0(x-W\varepsilon) \ge(1-A b^{-1/100})\bar g_0 \qquad(z\in U_b,\ x\in H). \label{eq:block-biased-sampler}$$ Define $$v_b(z)=\frac{F_b(t_z)}{p_b}\mathbf 1_{U_b}(z),\qquad g_b(x)=\max_{c\in C_b}v_b(x-c),\qquad \bar g_b=\mathbb E_{x\in G_b}g_b(x). \label{eq:block-line-weight}$$ These choices satisfy $$|\bar g_b-1|\le A b^{-1/100},\qquad 0\le g_b(x)\le\exp(5b^{0.56})\quad(x\in G_b),\qquad \left|\mathbb E_z F_b(t_z)\mathbf 1_{U_b}(z)-1\right| \le A b^{-1/20}. \label{eq:block-usable-bounds}$$ There is also a base version with no $H$, $g_0$, or $W$: take $U_b=E_b$ and choose $C_b$ so that the conclusions concerning $g_b$ in Equation [eq:block-usable-bounds] hold.

Let $L_b=\mathbb Z^b+C_b/p_b$. For $t\in\mathbb R^b$ put $k=\lfloor p_b t\rfloor\in\mathbb Z^b$ and $x=k\pmod{p_b}\in G_b$. Floors and fractional parts are taken coordinatewise. If $g_b(x)>0$, choose $c\in C_b$ attaining its maximum and let $z=x-c\in U_b$, again using standard representatives. Then $$\lambda=\frac{k-z}{p_b}\in L_b,\qquad
 \tau=t-\lambda=\frac{z+\{p_b t\}}{p_b}\in Q_z,\qquad
 g_b(x)=\frac{F_b(t_z)}{p_b}.
 \label{eq:block-cell-identity}$$ For all $\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}^b$, the point $\lambda+\varepsilon$ lies in $L_b$, its residual $t-\lambda-\varepsilon=\tau-\varepsilon$ has coordinates in $[-1,1]$, and $$\frac{h_b^b}{p_b}\gamma_b\bigl(h_b(t-\lambda-\varepsilon)\bigr)
       \ge e^{-\eta_b}g_b(x)P_{b,t_z}(\varepsilon).
 \label{eq:block-cell-lower}$$ The corresponding individual weight is at most $e^{-c b^{0.70}}$.

There are absolute constants $B,C,c,\kappa>0$ such that, for every integer $b_1\ge B$, the construction above has $$D\le C(b_1+1),\qquad
 R^2:=\sum_{i=1}^{r+1}b_i h_i^2
       \le C\bigl(b_1\log(b_1+1)+1\bigr).
 \label{eq:hierarchy-dimension-radius}$$ For every $y\in\mathbb R^D$ there is a finite nonempty pattern $\mathcal P_y\subset L$ such that $$\begin{aligned}
 \|(y-M\ell)_i\|_\infty&\le h_i
       \qquad(\ell\in\mathcal P_y,\ 1\le i\le r+1),
       \label{eq:hierarchy-residual}\\
 \sum_{\ell\in\mathcal P_y}D_v\gamma_D(y-M\ell)&\ge\kappa,
       \label{eq:hierarchy-total}\\
 \max_{\ell\in\mathcal P_y}D_v\gamma_D(y-M\ell)
       &\le \exp(-c b_1^{0.70}).
       \label{eq:hierarchy-cap}
\end{aligned}$$ The terminal block is constant on the pattern. For each ordinary block $i$ and each fixed suffix $(\ell_{i+1},\ldots,\ell_{r+1})$, its retained values belong to $\lambda_i+\{0,1\}^{b_i}$ for one $\lambda_i\in L_i$ depending on that suffix. In particular $|\mathcal P_y|\le 2^D$.*

*Order the scalar coordinates by increasing block index and denote them by $\ell[1],\ldots,\ell[D]$. Conditional on any fixed scalar suffix $\ell[j+1],\ldots,\ell[D]$, the possible next values $\ell[j]$ are at most two; if there are two, they differ by $1$. This property is preserved upon deleting any subset of the pattern.*


*If $y\in M[0,1)^D$, all raw coordinates can in addition be restricted to the fixed finite alphabets $$\begin{aligned}
 \ell_i&\in\bigl(p_i^{-1}\mathbb Z\cap[-Q_{\rm raw},Q_{\rm raw}]\bigr)^{b_i}
         &&(i\le r),\\
 \ell_{r+1}&\in\bigl(\mathbb Z\cap[-Q_{\rm raw},Q_{\rm raw}]\bigr)^T,
         &&Q_{\rm raw}=1+(D+2)^D.
 \end{aligned}
 \label{eq:hierarchy-alphabets}$$ For an ordinary block the logarithm of each scalar alphabet size is $O(D\log(D+2)+b_i\log b_i)$; the terminal version omits the second term. All implicit constants are absolute.

Let $K\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a convex body and $\Gamma$ a full-rank lattice. If its hole proportion $\delta=1-|\pi_\Gamma(K)|$ satisfies $$\delta<(1-\delta)k^{-n}$$ for a positive integer $k$, then $(1+1/k)K+\Gamma=\mathbb R^n$.

coverage.checked_domain: Every target for p in {2,3,5,7,31}, b in {1,2}; every scalar Boolean label at these primes. Invalid cases p=1,4,32 or b=0,3 are rejected.
coverage.oracle_basis: Independent exhaustive Boolean subset-sum image and native exact integer witness reconstruction; prime check independent of fmpz. The asymptotic covering theorem is outside this check.
